messages:
alex: quick UX thread — need input on guardrails for automatic degrade/rollback during rollouts. How should console + API surface triggers, actions, and audit? 

maria: what triggers are we supporting out of the box? error-rate, latency, model-quality? or custom metrics? 

alex: error-rate (5xx), p99 latency, household model quality regressions (eval set), and quota/exhaustion. thinking we should support multiple trigger types and composable rules. example proto:

```
{
  "auto_degrade": {
    "mode": "soft", // soft = throttle/switch variant, hard = full rollback
    "thresholds": [
      {"type": "error_rate", "window": "1m", "value": 0.03},
      {"type": "p99_latency", "window": "5m", "value_ms": 1200}
    ],
    "actions": ["switch_model","throttle","notify"],
    "audit_log": true
  }
}
```

sam: love the composable rules. UX note: show a single 'guardrail status' badge in the rollout timeline with hover details (which rule fired, when, metric snapshot). also allow pause + override buttons. 

jen: audit requirements — events must be immutable and show actor (auto | system | user), reason, metric snapshot, and pre/post config. retention 90d default, export to S3 for enterprise. 

noah: telemetry names: `rollout.guardrail.fired`, `rollout.guardrail.action_taken`, `rollout.guardrail.duration_ms`. include labels: model_id, route, canary_percent, triggered_by_metric. 

ops-bot: [alert] canary deploy 1887654321-1 for model:open-llama-30b -- healthcheck status: failing (error_rate=0.078) :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: started canary 50rps -> 10% traffic

deploy-bot: canary failed — auto_degrade rule fired: switch_model -> fallback:open-llama-30b-quant (action_by=system) 

maria: question: should API expose 'dry_run' for auto_degrade so customers can test rules without taking action? 

alex: yes — exposing dry_run + backtest on historical traces is useful. UI should show suggested actions with confidence score before enabling. 

sam: permissioning: only rollout owners + org-admins can toggle automatic actions; others can file a request that appears in the timeline. 

jen: add an 'audit-accept' flow so someone can retroactively approve an auto action for compliance — but keep the event immutable. 

noah: implementation note: make guardrail evaluation idempotent and emit deterministic UUID for each evaluation for traceability. 

alex: next steps: i'll mock the badge + timeline panel, maria can draft API contract (include dry_run, actions[], retention), noah will add telemetry events, jen will spec audit retention/export, sam will draft the permission matrix. sync EOW. :thumbsup:
